legend: There are n$$$n$$$ crossings in Bytetown, connected with m$$$m$$$ bidirectional roads. The i$$$i$$$-th road connects crossings ui$$$u_i$$$ and vi$$$v_i$$$, has length of li$$$l_i$$$ meters and a cost factor of ci$$$c_i$$$.

In order to ease the road traffic, a special fine system is used in Bytetown. You can drive with any speed and change the speed whenever you want. However, if the maximum speed during your travel along the road i$$$i$$$ is v$$$v$$$ meters per second, you should pay v⋅ci$$$v \cdot c_i$$$ dollars fine.

You live near the crossing 1$$$1$$$ and want to get to the crossing n$$$n$$$ in no more than T$$$T$$$ seconds. What is the smallest possible fine you will have to pay if you choose the route and the speed for each road optimally?
input: In the first line of the input there are three numbers n$$$n$$$, m$$$m$$$ and T$$$T$$$ (1≤n≤2000$$$1 \leq n \leq 2000$$$, 1≤m≤100000$$$1 \leq m \leq 100\,000$$$, 1≤T≤109$$$1 \leq T \leq 10^9$$$).

The i$$$i$$$-th of the next m$$$m$$$ lines contains four numbers ui$$$u_i$$$, vi$$$v_i$$$, li$$$l_i$$$, ci$$$c_i$$$, describing the i$$$i$$$-th edge according to the statement (1≤ui,vi≤n$$$1 \leq u_i, v_i \leq n$$$, ui≠vi$$$u_i \neq v_i$$$, 1≤li,ci≤109$$$1 \leq l_i, c_i \leq 10^9$$$).
It is guaranteed that it is possible to reach the crossing n$$$n$$$ starting at the crossing 1$$$1$$$.
output: Print single real number — the smallest possible fine. Your answer will be considered correct if its relative or absolute error doesn't exceed 10−6$$$10^{-6}$$$.
